dishes.name: St. Galler Bratwurst
dishes.desc: Pale veal and pork sausage with a protected geographical status, eaten without mustard. The city's butchers set its rules as early as 1438.

dishes.name: St. Galler Bürli
dishes.desc: Crusty bread rolls baked in pairs that are pulled apart. The traditional partner of the St. Galler Bratwurst.

dishes.name: St. Galler Biber
dishes.desc: Honey gingerbread filled with almond paste, pressed in carved moulds. Sold by the city's bakers as the local sweet.

dishes.name: St. Galler Fladen
dishes.desc: Flat fruit tart, the traditional pastry of the Eastern Swiss countryside around St. Gallen. Bakeries and chocolatiers sell it by the slice.

dishes.name: Galler Sammetsuppe
dishes.desc: Smooth and velvety soup, an old St. Gallen dish. A few traditional restaurants in the old town still make it.
